assertions_evaluated.text: Rule file follows the Description-Incorrect-Correct template (title, description, ## Incorrect, ## Correct)
assertions_evaluated.evidence: File has title, opening description paragraph, '## Incorrect' and '## Correct' sections plus '## Enforcement'/'## Why'

assertions_evaluated.text: Description states WHAT the rule enforces and WHY, in imperative language (MUST/NEVER, not 'try to' or 'consider')
assertions_evaluated.evidence: 'Claude MUST first run `git status` and `git diff`... never assume it maps to wipe the whole file's working-tree state'

assertions_evaluated.text: Incorrect example shows the plausible `git checkout -- <path>` mistake without a prior `git status`, not a contrived variant

assertions_evaluated.text: Correct example is the minimal fix of the same scenario (checks status / confirms before discarding), not a rewritten unrelated scenario
assertions_evaluated.evidence: Correct section runs git status/git diff on the same file/scenario, then asks the user when more than one change is uncommitted

assertions_evaluated.text: Rule body contains no numbered steps or multi-step procedural content
assertions_evaluated.evidence: Body uses prose + code-block dialogue transcripts, no numbered step list
